title: Quarterly governance & cadence for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Tomás Rivera
description: Create a repeatable quarterly planning and governance playbook that aligns Hosted API product priorities with the Model Catalog lifecycle. This ticket scopes the plan: intake rubric for model curation, OKR mapping for quarterly goals, rollout gates (canary -> staged -> global), deprecation/retirement rules, cost and latency guardrails, and the communication cadence across Product, Engineering, Research, and Solutions. The deliverable is a documented playbook, a calendar of planning rituals, and a minimal set of templates (intake form, OKR mapping template, risk buffer worksheet).
goals: Define intake rubric for new models and model variants (privacy, cost, latency, eval pass/fail)
Map hosted API product OKRs to model catalog outcomes (quality, cost-per-token, availability)
Set quarterly release cadence and model rotation windows with buffer months for rollback
Establish SLO/alert requirements and telemetry baseline to gate model promotion
Create an operational deprecation policy and customer communication template
milestones: M1: Intake rubric + scoring matrix drafted (due 2026-03-22)
M2: OKR mapping and target metrics agreed with Eng & Research (due 2026-04-05)
M3: Release cadence calendar published and integrated into cycle planning (due 2026-04-19)
M4: Canary gating playbook + rollback checklist tested in staging (due 2026-05-03)
M5: Final playbook reviewed and communicated to GTM and Support (due 2026-05-15)
acceptance_criteria: A1: Intake rubric includes mandatory fields and a pass/fail threshold for hosted inclusion
A2: OKR mapping doc links to measurable targets (latency P50/P95, cost-per-1k tokens, eval pass rate)
A3: Release cadence has clear freeze windows and a documented emergency rollback path
A4: Telemetry dashboards exist for model-level cost and quality and are reachable from Console links
A5: Playbook has a communication template for customers and internal status updates
tasks: T1: Interview Eng leads on current model onboarding bottlenecks
T2: Draft intake rubric and scoring matrix (collab Confluence doc)
T3: Workshop OKR mapping with Research, Eng infra, and DX (two sessions)
T4: Draft canary gating checklist and failure modes with SRE
T5: Create sample rollout calendar and publish to shared calendar
T6: Run one simulated model promotion in staging to validate gating and dashboards
T7: Prepare comms/email + support playbook for deprecation scenarios
risks: R1: Insufficient telemetry granularity prevents accurate cost-per-model attribution
R2: Tight quarterly cadence may cause rushed promotions and quality regressions
R3: Cross-team dependencies (SRE/Research) may delay gating automation
R4: Customers on Dedicated may require separate deprecation timelines
R5: Ambiguous ownership of model evaluation thresholds will create disputes during triage

decisions: D1: Use a numeric score (0-100) in the intake rubric; >=70 required for hosted inclusion
D2: Cadence set to monthly model promotion windows with one reserved buffer month per quarter
D3: Canary rollouts will use staged traffic 1% -> 10% -> 50% with automated health checks
D4: Dedicated and Private deployments will be offered a 2-quarter lag for deprecation notices
